subtopic: Repurchase Limits and Pro Rata Allocation
source_evidence: If shareholder requests for repurchase exceed the amount of outstanding shares eligible for repurchase during a repurchase offer, repurchase is generally done on a pro rata basis.
answer: Interval funds limit how many shares they repurchase during each offer: the source says the limit is 5% to 25% of all outstanding shares. If shareholders collectively request more shares than the amount eligible for repurchase, the fund generally allocates the available repurchases on a pro rata basis. As a result, a shareholder may be able to sell back only part of the shares they requested to have repurchased; the full requested amount is not guaranteed.
